claims.statement: Beyond a certain number of options, more options make people less satisfied with the option they choose (more options help up to a point, then satisfaction falls).

claims.statement: Beyond a certain number of options, more options make people more likely to put off choosing or to choose nothing at all.
claims.exposure: more options beyond a certain number

claims.statement: Committing to a choice that cannot be undone makes people more satisfied with it than keeping the option to change their mind.
claims.exposure: a final, irreversible choice (closing the other options)
claims.comparison: a choice one can still reverse

claims.statement: Having more freedom of choice in one's life makes people less happy overall.
claims.exposure: more freedom of choice in life

notFound: no multi-lab replication of choice overload; one single-lab preregistered null (lindkvist-2022-donation); Ariga 2018 (10.1109/kst.2018.8426193) not read
no meta-analysis of choice overload since Chernev 2015 except the reanalysis by McShane & Böckenholt 2018
no direct replication of Iyengar & Lepper 2000 nor of Gilbert & Ebert 2002 among the citing works read; no meta-analysis of decision reversibility
no Egyptian or Arab sample on the number of options, choice deferral, reversibility or maximizing; Arab samples only on autonomy (zayed-2026-autonomy)
not read in full (closed): Chernev 2015 p. 348 (which corrected coefficient is the unmoderated mean), Hu 2026
not kept, no abstract or no result sentence: Bullens 2011 and 2013, Verme 2009, Abdur Rahman & Veenhoven 2017, Shah & Wolford 2007, Iyengar & Kamenica 2010
the book's own text of ch. 8 is not public: the idea is taken from the author's 2019 article that restates it

found.note: Chernev corrigendum, not linked by Crossref: the mean-effect section holds b = .17 and .41 (p < .001) but also b = .04 (p > .4). Chernev is now read as an effect under conditions, not as a meta-analysis that contradicts Scheibehenne on the average
reanalysis (Böckenholt co-author of Chernev): the effect varies by outcome measure, so c1 (satisfaction) and c2 (deferral) cannot rest on one pooled figure
the card line pooled « satisfaction » alone: the mean covers satisfaction or the wish to choose; a mean near zero alone reads as ❌ under a ⚖️, so Chernev's condition is written under it
inverted U, with reutskaja-2018-neural: c1 and c2 rewritten with Manson's own « beyond a certain point »; the monotone version was stronger than the book
randomized, Hong Kong, 652 adults: 4 or 16 self-care exercises beat 1 on practice and decision satisfaction; no loss up to 16
preregistered: donating did not change from 2 to 80 charities, whatever preference certainty: against c2 and against Chernev's preference-uncertainty moderator
six nations, 7,436 people: too little choice is the norm outside the US and weighs more on satisfaction than too much; by Iyengar and Schwartz themselves
meta-analysis, 63 countries, 420,599 people: more individualism goes with more well-being: c4 moves from mixed to contradicts (association, autonomy rather than number of options)
the only Arab sample found (328 Arabic-speaking adults): personal autonomy goes with less distress (cross-sectional); nothing Arab on the number of options, deferral or reversibility
field + preregistered (669): telling people they may choose as much as they wish raises satisfaction with what they chose: nuances c3 and c4
support for c3 the draft had missed: acts of closure raise satisfaction with choices from large sets (4 studies, consumer choices, no replication)
support for c2 in a real decision (South Africa, randomized mailers): fewer example loans, more take-up; an advertisement, not a choice set
the jam study enters content/contested.json (average near zero, failed tests, a preregistered null; no multi-lab replication) and is no longer counted as evidence: never shown as a fact
risk of bias found in the full text (manipulation check d reported as 0.98 for means implying about 10; dummy coding written both ways): kept, weighed less
Hu, Moon & VanEpps 2026, six preregistered experiments (10,092 US adults) whose premise is that larger sets yield better-liked choices; full text not read: not used
Roets, Schwartz & Guan 2012: maximizers report less well-being only in choice-rich societies (US, Western Europe), not in China; the one limited support for c4, Schwartz co-author; not added
Altinger 2025, 402 US physicians, randomized: more alternatives meant less status quo, not more deferral (1 vs 2-4 options); not added
Chirkov 2003 (incl. Turkey) and Welzel & Inglehart 2010 (about 80 societies): autonomy or agency goes with well-being; same direction as c4's contradiction, not added

counterEvidence.conclusion: ⚖️ low holds: no claim reaches a net moderate direction. Taken: c1/c2 rewritten with « beyond a certain point » and read as « near zero on average, present under conditions »; the jam study is contested and no longer evidence; c4 now contradicts (63-country meta-analysis, the only Arab sample); Gu 2013 added for c3, Li 2022 weighed less; card line widened, with its condition.
